title: If the dying person was one of those brought near...
subtitle: The three groups return, at the moment of death
then: Ibn Kathir says these are {idea}the three conditions people face upon their death{/idea}, the same three groups from the surah's opening. Those brought near fulfilled the obligations and the recommended acts, and avoided even some allowed things.
now: The surah began with the end of the world. It ends with the end of one person: someone you know, maybe you. {idea}The same three groups, now in a single bedroom.{/idea}
old: The Day is far away; death is just an ending.
new: Death is the first moment I learn which group I'm in.
try: Do one good act today that is not required: two extra rakat, a charity, a few minutes of dhikr.

title: For them: rest, provision, and a Garden of Delight.
subtitle: The good news given at death
then: Ibn Abbas said Rawh means rest and Rayhan a place of rest; others said mercy, joy and provision. The angels bring {reward}this good news at death{/reward}. The Prophet ﷺ said whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him, and explained that this news is what makes the believer love it.
now: You tense up at funerals and steer away from the topic. {trap}Death feels like only loss.{/trap} {reward}For the believer, it opens with rest and a welcome.{/reward}
old: Death is just loss and darkness.
new: For those near to Allah, death opens with rest and good news.
try: Ask Allah today: make the best of my days the day I meet You.

title: And if the dying one was among the people of the right...
subtitle: The ordinary believer's moment
then: Ibn Kathir describes this as the dying person who is {reward}among those on the right{/reward}, the believers just below the nearest in rank. The surah gives them their own moment, separate from the foremost.
now: You are probably not the most devoted person in your mosque. You try, you fall short, you come back. {reward}The verse sets a moment aside for people like you.{/reward}
old: The beautiful deathbed scenes are for very pious people.
new: Ordinary believers on the right have their own welcome.
try: Keep up one small good habit today that you would love to die upon.

title: Peace to you, you are of the people of the right.
subtitle: The angels' greeting at the last moment
then: Ikrimah said {reward}the angels will greet him with salam{/reward} and tell him he is among those on the right. Ibn Kathir calls this a good explanation and links it to the verse where angels descend saying: fear not, and do not grieve.
now: You wait outside an exam hall, nervous, and a friend comes out smiling: you passed. The relief is everything. {reward}This salam is that, at the end of a whole life.{/reward}
old: My last moments will be full of fear.
new: For the people of the right, the last words heard are peace.
try: Give salam to three people today, fully and warmly.

title: But if he was among the deniers who went astray...
subtitle: The third group, at death

row.title: it can be reversed
sub: while the soul is in the body

then: Ibn Kathir describes them as {trap}those who denied the truth, were led astray from guidance{/trap}, and did not know Allah. The same two words, deniers and astray, were used for the people of the left earlier in the surah.
now: It begins with small choices: ignoring a reminder, mocking someone who prays, telling yourself it is all made up. {idea}While you are alive, every one of those can be reversed.{/idea}
old: Denial is just a personal opinion with no consequences.
new: Denial has an end point, and I can turn back before it.
try: If you have mocked or brushed off faith recently, ask Allah's forgiveness for it today.

title: Their welcome is boiling water.
subtitle: A guest's welcome, turned to punishment
then: The word nuzul, a guest's welcome, appears again. Ibn Kathir says he is received {trap}as a guest, with Hamim{/trap}, boiling water. The near are welcomed with rest. The deniers' welcome is the reverse.
now: You know how it feels to arrive somewhere you are not wanted. {idea}The verse is a warning to make sure you arrive as a welcome guest{/idea}, and there is still time to prepare.
old: I'll worry about the next life later.
new: My welcome there depends on how I live here.
try: Make one sincere tawbah today for something specific.

title: And entry into the blazing Fire.
subtitle: The final end of denial
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}he will reside in Hellfire{/trap}. The verse is short and sober. It completes the three endings: rest for the near, peace for the right, and this for those who denied.
now: You might feel this verse land on you as you think of things you have done. {idea}That feeling is a mercy, not a sentence.{/idea} {reward}While you breathe, the door of repentance is open.{/reward}
old: I've done too much wrong; this verse is about me.
new: This verse warns me while I can still turn, and that is mercy.
try: Say astaghfirullah wa atubu ilayh sincerely three times today.

title: This is the certain truth.
subtitle: No doubt, no escape, no exception
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}this news is the truth; there is no doubt about it, nor escape from it for anyone{/idea}. The surah opened by saying no one would deny the Event when it comes. It closes by calling all of it certain.
now: You hold many things as certain: the sunrise, the date your rent is due, that you will get older. {idea}This verse adds one more to that list.{/idea}
old: The afterlife is something I hope is true.
new: The afterlife is as certain as anything I know.
try: Write one sentence about the Day as a certainty and keep it where you will see it.

title: End with praise: glorify your Lord, the Most Great.
subtitle: The surah closes the way the signs closed
then: After the certain truth comes the command: {reward}glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great{/reward}. The Prophet ﷺ said two phrases are light on the tongue, heavy on the Balance, and loved by the Most Merciful: glory be to Allah and with His praise, glory be to Allah the Magnificent.
now: At a red light, in the lift, waiting for the kettle. Ten seconds you usually give to your phone. {reward}Two light phrases fit there.{/reward}
old: Remembering Allah needs a special time and place.
new: Two short phrases, said anywhere, are heavy on the Balance.
try: Say subhanAllahi wa bihamdihi, subhanAllahil Azim at one red light or queue today.
